title: What is the Role of Structure for Glasses?
content: Glasses pose many unique scientific and engineering problems. At some level, physicists still don't understand the nature of the glass 'transition'. When a crystal solidifies from a melt, long-range periodic order emerges. In contrast, glasses solidify with the disordered structure of the liquid. Crystals deform via the creation and propagation of dislocations that are defects or tears in the order parameter field. For glasses, the structural transformations that mediate deformation, and give rise to their brittle mechanical failure are not known. Moreover, strikingly similar glassy behavior is seen at multiple length scales, from glasses composed of atoms to colloidal glasses to granular assemblies. How can we understand the role structure plays in the nature and properties of glass?
